question.problem: Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables, and suppose $\text{E}[X∣Y]=2Y-2.$ If $\text{E}[X]=8,$ what is $\text{E}[Y]?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given an expression for $\text{E}[X∣Y]$ in terms of $Y,$ and the value of $\text{E}[X].$ This is a direct application of the tower property, which states that

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\text{E}[X∣Y]].
$$

So, we substitute the given expression for the inner expectation, which gives

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[2Y-2].
$$

Now, we apply the linearity of expectation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\text{E}[2Y-2] \\  & =2\cdot \text{E}[Y]-2\end{aligned}
$$

We are told that $\text{E}[X]=8,$ so we solve this equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =2\cdot \text{E}[Y]-2 \\ 10 & =2\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\ \text{E}[Y] & =5\end{aligned}
$$
